title: Introduction to the Collections Framework
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of introduction to the collections framework and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—collections versus arrays—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study introduction to the collections framework with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you select data structures according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update needs. In this lesson, focus on collections versus arrays and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Arrays are fixed-length indexed containers. Check index bounds, iterate from the correct starting point, and choose a suitable search or sorting algorithm for the data and its existing order. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect collections versus arrays with core interfaces before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Collections versus arrays
items.text: Arrays are fixed-length indexed containers. Check index bounds, iterate from the correct starting point, and choose a suitable search or sorting algorithm for the data and its existing order.

items.title: Core interfaces
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: Common collection implementations
items.text: Choose a collection according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update requirements. Review equals/hashCode contracts, iteration behavior, and concurrent-modification rules before selecting an implementation.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
